# AIOX Architect Activator

## When To Use
Use for system architecture (fullstack, backend, frontend, infrastructure), technology stack selection (technical evaluation), API design (REST/GraphQL/tRPC/WebSocket), security architecture, performance optimization,...

## Activation Protocol
1. Load `.aiox-core/development/agents/architect.md` as source of truth (fallback: `.codex/agents/architect.md`).
2. Adopt this agent persona and command system.
3. Generate greeting via `node .aiox-core/development/scripts/generate-greeting.js architect` and show it first.
4. Stay in this persona until the user asks to switch or exit.

## Starter Commands
- `*help` - Show all available commands with descriptions
- `*create-full-stack-architecture` - Complete system architecture
- `*create-backend-architecture` - Backend architecture design
- `*create-front-end-architecture` - Frontend architecture design
- `*document-project` - Generate project documentation
- `*research` - Generate deep research prompt
- `*analyze-project-structure` - Analyze project for new feature implementation (WIS-15)
- `*guide` - Show comprehensive usage guide for this agent

## Non-Negotiables
- Follow `.aiox-core/constitution.md`.
- Execute workflows/tasks only from declared dependencies.
- Do not invent requirements outside the project artifacts.

  void observeRequestBytes(java.util.function.Consumer<byte[]> observer) {
    this.requestBytesObserver = observer;
  }

  private java.util.function.Consumer<byte[]> requestBytesObserver;

  @Override
  public DispatchOutcome send(RunJob job) {
    String misconfiguration = misconfiguration();
    if (misconfiguration != null) {
      // The execution id is the only job field named: the body carries resolved secrets.
      LOGGER.warn(
          "Dispatch of execution {} refused before sending: {}",
          job.executionId(),
          misconfiguration);
      job.resolvedSecrets().values().forEach(com.citi.put.checks.studio.secrets.SecretValue::close);
      return DispatchOutcome.refusedTerminal(misconfiguration);
    }
    HttpRequest request;
    byte[] requestBytes = null;
    try {
      requestBytes =
          com.citi.put.checks.studio.secrets.SecretWireWriter.bytes(
              objectMapper, job.observed() == null ? body(job) : observedBody(job));
      request =
          HttpRequest.newBuilder(
                  URI.create(
                      job.observed() == null
                          ? runner.runsUrl()
                          : runner.baseUrl().replaceAll("/+$", "") + "/v2/runs"))
              .timeout(properties.admissionTimeoutOrDefault())
              .header("Content-Type", "application/json")
              .header("Authorization", "Bearer " + runner.serviceIdentityToken())
              .POST(HttpRequest.BodyPublishers.ofByteArray(requestBytes))
              .build();
    } catch (IOException | RuntimeException e) {
      if (requestBytes != null) java.util.Arrays.fill(requestBytes, (byte) 0);
      job.resolvedSecrets().values().forEach(com.citi.put.checks.studio.secrets.SecretValue::close);
      return DispatchOutcome.refusedTerminal("the run job could not be serialized");
    }

    HttpResponse<String> response;
    try {
      if (requestBytesObserver != null) requestBytesObserver.accept(requestBytes);
      response = httpClient.send(request, HttpResponse.BodyHandlers.ofString());
    } catch (HttpTimeoutException e) {
      return DispatchOutcome.ambiguous("timeout");
    } catch (IOException e) {
      return DispatchOutcome.ambiguous("connection loss");
    } catch (InterruptedException e) {
      Thread.currentThread().interrupt();
      return DispatchOutcome.ambiguous("interrupted");
    } finally {
      java.util.Arrays.fill(requestBytes, (byte) 0);
    }
    if (response.statusCode() == 429 && metrics != null) {
      metrics.recordRefusal();
    }
    return classify(
        response.statusCode(), response.headers().firstValue("Retry-After").orElse(null));
  }

  /**
   * {@code DELETE /v1/runs/{executionId}} with the same base URL and the same bearer as {@link
   * #send} (Studio v1 WP4). No body, no redirect followed, no automatic retry: the dispatcher's
   * next pass is the retry, and it happens only for an outcome that did not {@linkplain
   * CancelOutcome#settled() settle}.
   */
  @Override
  public CancelOutcome cancel(UUID executionId) {
    String misconfiguration = misconfiguration();
    if (misconfiguration != null) {
      LOGGER.warn("Cancel of execution {} not relayed: {}", executionId, misconfiguration);
      return CancelOutcome.FAILED;
    }
    HttpRequest request =
        HttpRequest.newBuilder(URI.create(runner.runUrl(executionId)))
            .timeout(properties.admissionTimeoutOrDefault())
            .header("Authorization", "Bearer " + runner.serviceIdentityToken())
            .DELETE()
            .build();
    int status;
    try {
      status = httpClient.send(request, HttpResponse.BodyHandlers.discarding()).statusCode();
    } catch (IOException e) {
      LOGGER.warn("Cancel of execution {} not relayed: {}", executionId, e.getClass().getName());
      return CancelOutcome.FAILED;
    } catch (InterruptedException e) {
      Thread.currentThread().interrupt();
      return CancelOutcome.FAILED;
    }
    return classifyCancel(status);
  }

  /** The cancel classification table, extracted like {@link #classify} so a test can drive it. */
  public static CancelOutcome classifyCancel(int status) {
    return switch (status) {
      case 202 -> CancelOutcome.ACKNOWLEDGED;
      case 409 -> CancelOutcome.ALREADY_FINISHED;
      case 404 -> CancelOutcome.NOT_FOUND;
      default -> CancelOutcome.FAILED;
    };
  }

  private String misconfiguration() {
    if (runner == null || !runner.isConfigured()) {
      return RUNNER_NOT_CONFIGURED;
    }
    if (!runner.hasServiceIdentity()) {
      return SERVICE_IDENTITY_NOT_CONFIGURED;
    }
    return null;
  }

### What the code does today (design §1, condensed)

Guided input kinds are `nonsecretText | destination` and require a value. `GuidedSourceClassifier` already parses `<secret ID>` and requires it declared but emits configuration references only for `var`; the change is emission, not parsing. Every guided start fails `AUTH_CONNECTION_REQUIRED`. `knownSecrets` is always `[]`; the collector merges/withholds and wipes on dispose; sanitizer bound 64 × 4096. The collector **never exports a password control as a node** — hence the node-free target. The ordinary dispatch pass resolves secrets at dispatch only, erases on every exit path, carries `secretOrigins`; it has no password-only rule and no login detection. The observed replay job carries `accountHandle`; V33 DB functions require account fields; `AWAITING_AUTH` is in the V30 CHECK. `translation.enabled` is dead unless set (two gates). No production guided data exists; publication and observed replay default off; the guided worker has no `CMD`/chart (OBS-009).

### Target flow (design §2)

```
author: "Enter <var USER> as username" / "Enter <secret PASS> as password" / "Click Sign in" / "Open reports"
  classify  → sourceReference{kind:secretRef, intendedSlot:fill.value, referenceName:PASS}; preflight mayUse + exists, no read
  plan      → model sees step text with the token span masked, the reference (ID), never a value
  materialize → authoredInputs += {kind:secretRef, secretId:PASS} (no value; hashed into authoredInputsHash)
  propose   → fill.value={kind:secretRef, sourceInputId}, target={kind:passwordControl, documentId, generation}
  prepare   → mayUse recheck (names only); trusted runner pins exactly one visible enabled input[type=password]
  dispatch  → backend resolve() from Vault (CSI/env/testId/principal), RELEASE audit row, BridgeDispatch.secret on mTLS bridge, erase
  act       → same pinned element re-proven in-world (attached, type=password, unique, origin, form.action), withhold BEFORE fill, fill via handle
  observe   → next observation is the reached document; knownSecrets scrubs any echo
  publish   → artifact fill value {kind:secretRef, sourceInputId}; inputRecipes {kind:secretRef, referenceName:PASS}; no value anywhere
  replay    → job.secrets/secretOrigins resolved per run (ordinary dispatch pass), same origin + password rule in the observed adapter, model-free
  stop      → knownSecrets = [], inventory disposed, dispatch frame not retained
```

### Codes introduced or removed

| Code | Where | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `SECRET_UNAVAILABLE` (404-class), `SECRET_USE_NOT_AUTHORIZED` (403), `SECRET_USE_REVOKED` (409), `VAULT_UNAVAILABLE` (503) | guided `error`/`result` | Draft/authorization facts; never a value |
| `LOGIN_REQUIRED` + `detail:{stepId, loginStepsPresent}` | guided result; replay `x-runner-error-codes` | Annotation of an existing failure (§5) |
| `PASSWORD_TARGET_ABSENT`, `PASSWORD_TARGET_AMBIGUOUS` | guided `POLICY_DENIED` reasons; replay `POLICY_REFUSED` | 0 or >1 candidates, nothing typed |
| `TARGET_CHANGED` (existing ledger outcome) | guided fill | pinned element no longer the same attached unique password input |
| `PASSWORD_FORM_ACTION_NOT_ALLOWED` | guided fill refusal | owning `form.action` origin outside `allowedOrigins` |
| `PASSWORD_CONTROL_READ_REFUSED` | observed executor (learn, replay) | value read on a password control |
| `SECRET_TOO_LONG` | dispatch | stored entry > 4096; never truncated |
| `IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT` (existing) | runner replay map | same body, different `secret.secretId` |
| `CONFIGURATION_DENIED` (existing) | guided mode start | `capacity ≠ 1` with secret fills enabled (if that branch is chosen) |
| `REVOKED` | `bridge#stop` reason; `ExecutionControl.revoked` | mid-run revocation |

### Trust boundaries in one paragraph (design §4)

The gateway sees IDs, never values (structural: the kind has no `value` field). The DB stores IDs, vault version identifiers and audit rows. The only value-bearing channels are `BridgeDispatch.secret` (guided, mTLS + RS256) and `Launch3/Execute3.secrets` (replay, the backend→runner hop that OBS-009 makes TLS with client-certificate authentication). Runner memory holds the value from the dispatch frame until `withhold` copies it into the private inventory; wiped at `dispose`/`stop`; no scratch file, argv or env ever carries it. The browser profile is a separate disk sink neutralised by the pre-written `Preferences` file and canary-scanned. Video shows masked dots only (password-only rule); a page that later echoes a secret in plain text is a stated residual. Runner free-text sinks pass a redactor built from resolved values. Transport gates G-1 (guided mTLS), G-2 (no real credential in Vault until every secret-bearing hop is TLS-authenticated) and G-3 (no scheduled secret-referencing run before production background/secret-use authorization sources exist) are OBS-009/OBS-010 items and are **not** closed by this story.

## Production seams and additional implementation cautions

1. `GuidedDispatchService.java:80-104` consumes/commits before constructing/sending an ephemeral frame and rejects ambient transactions. Preserve at-most-once and no outbox. Recovery tests must never resend an already-consumed action to obtain a passing proof.
2. `StudioDispatcher.java:320-367` has ordinary scoped resolution/close on failure. `:380-426` is currently a separate observed branch: it neither resolves secrets nor follows ordinary definite-refusal retry semantics. AC-7/13 must actually change this branch; a passing legacy C-4 is insufficient.
3. `VaultStudioReferenceResolver.java:63-94` preflight currently reads secret values and erases them. Names-only start/prepare must use a scoped existence/metadata seam instead; `StudioVaultProvider` currently has read/list but no explicit exists method. Authorized-start/prepare read counter must also be zero, not just the already-denied case. No secret bytes may enter classifier, prompt or session row during existence checking.
4. `RunJob.java:78-83,123-155` retains a deep-copied observed JsonNode, and `HttpRunnerDispatchClient.java:105-116` serializes `job.observed()` directly for observed jobs. Replacing only `resolvedSecrets` and the ordinary body writer leaves this observed value-bearing envelope exposed to record-toString/Jackson copying. AC-9's single SecretValue writer and all-value-free printable guarantee must cover the actual observed envelope and exception paths.
5. Collector `:35-41,504-515,544-560` already tracks mutation revision and complete candidate-universe guards. The new resolver must retain these guards: a currently attached handle alone cannot detect detach/re-attach between prepare and fill. Do not assert uniqueness from a truncated/budget-exhausted count. Overflow or unknown traversal completeness must refuse, never clamp to a usable count. Existing fill `:667-677` rechecks after synchronous focus; new password fill must preserve that check and `/trap` zero-typing proof.
6. `observedReplayAdapter.ts:17` creates observations with `knownSecrets:[]` today; it must receive/withhold actual secrets before actions and sanitize every following observation. Rotation/isolation canaries must exercise that actual adapter, not substitute fake observation exports.
7. `HashicorpStudioVaultProvider.java:350` parses a tree, both wire clients use ofString, create bound remains 8192, control service has cancellation only, and translation has false defaults/two absent matchIfMissing gates. These are accurately specified required changes, not evidence already implemented.
8. V34 is free at review time. V33 has exact v2 SQL predicates and closed coverage keys (D5). Profile split remains necessary: observed/publication configuration is !worker, while readiness injects verifier optionally. Setter is not dead code.
9. C-7 backend and C-12 backend are this story's obligations; UI/MSW/explanation render remains OBS-008. C-8/9/10 and human video masking are OBS-009/010. Preserve all external G-1/2/3 gates and stated JVM/JS/TLS, video echo, whole-origin trust and Vault version-history residuals.
10. AC-14 retention default is unchanged. Root/architect RULING-5 selects monthly partitions keyed by immutable `release_occurred_at`; USAGE carries the RELEASE timestamp so both remain in the same retention month, while `occurred_at` records actual event time. The existing twelve-month pruner performs detach/drop. An immutable insert trigger plus transactional lock validates the full scoped RELEASE locator; actual session/admission/execution FKs remain. AC-14 does not require an audit self-FK, and no self-FK is claimed. Ordinary UPDATE/DELETE remain refused; controlled partition ownership/retention role must not grant generic DELETE authority. RELEASE→USAGE locator writes remain append-only and insertion must enforce identical scope/attempt/secret/coordinate and duplicate refusal. Cross-month retention must not orphan retained USAGE, block approved expiry indefinitely or allow mismatched links. DDL/FK strategy remains a data-engineer implementation choice under these invariants; require actual PostgreSQL missing/wrong-scope/duplicate/concurrent USAGE refusal, cross-month alignment and detach/drop retention oracles alongside SEC-9/C-11. A USAGE referencing a pruned RELEASE must fail, and no retained USAGE may outlive its RELEASE partition. This does not change Q3's window.

## Completion boundary

Remaining DDL clarification (AC-13/14/19, C-4/C-11): the write-once `REVOKED_MID_RUN` authorization decision must coexist with exactly one terminal USAGE summary for each RELEASE. Architect/data-engineer must explicitly define its row kind, affected-release link, decision-stage discriminator and uniqueness key before V34 SQL edits. The proposed separate LIVE_RECHECK authorization-decision RELEASE linked to the prior resolved RELEASE is acceptable in principle only if it records no send/value, does not replace the original resolution fact, creates no second terminal USAGE, preserves the complete scoped locator/retention month, and repeated/concurrent sweep/control checks cannot duplicate the event. This remaining data-model clarification does not affect independent Lane C contract construction and is not claimed closed by this review. Root owns its pre-DDL hold and durable amendment.

## Story

As a Studio author, I want to write login steps that reference my saved credentials as `<secret ID>` — exactly as `<var NAME>` works for nonsecret values — and have the guided first Run and later model-free replays fill them only into the one password control at the one moment the step calls for, so that login-protected pages can be tested on the single observed path without any account provider while no credential is ever shown, stored outside Vault, or logged.
